source_text:
Εἰ οὖν οἱ ἐν παλαιοῖς πράγμασιν ἀναστραφέντες εἰς καινότητα ἐλπίδος ἦλθον, μηκέτι σαββατίζοντες, ἀλλὰ κατὰ κυριακὴν ζῶντες, ἐν ᾗ καὶ ἡ ζωὴ ἡμῶν ἀνέτειλεν δἰ αὐτοῦ καὶ τοῦ θανάτου αὐτοῦ, ὅν τινες ἀρνοῦνται, δἰ οὗ μυστηρίου ἐλάβομεν τὸ πιστεύειν, καὶ διὰ τοῦτο ὑπομένομεν, ἵνα εὑρεθῶμεν μαθηταὶ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ τοῦ μόνου διδασκάλου ἡμῶν:
πῶς ἡμεῖς δυνησόμεθα ζῆσαι χωρὶς αὐτοῦ, οὗ καὶ οἱ προφῆται μαθηταὶ ὄντες τῷ πνεύματι ὡς διδάσκαλον αὐτὸν προσεδόκων; καὶ διὰ τοῦτο, ὃν δικαίως ἀνέμενον, παρὼν ἤγειρεν αὐτοὺς ἐκ νεκρῶν.
thought_title: The prophets lived by the Lord's Day and awaited Christ
orientation: Ignatius is writing to the Magnesians, arguing that Christians must no longer live according to Judaism but according to Christ, who is the new hope.
pass_a_gloss: If therefore the [ones] in old things having conducted themselves into newness of hope came, no longer sabbath-keeping, but according to [the] Lord's [day] living, in which also the life of us dawned through him and through the death of him, which some deny, through which mystery we received faith, and because of this we endure, in order that we may be found disciples of Jesus Christ the only teacher of us: how will we be able to live without him, whom also the prophets disciples being in the spirit as teacher him awaited? and because of this, whom righteously they awaited, having come he raised them from [the] dead.

choices.why: The adjective κυριακή is used substantivally for the Lord's day (Sunday), contrasting with Sabbath-keeping; the literal rendering preserves the contrast with σαββατίζοντες.
The verb means to rise or spring up, used of the sun; 'dawned' captures the image of life arising through Christ.
The articular infinitive expresses the act or capacity of believing; 'the ability to believe' makes the reception of faith explicit.

choices.term: μαθηταὶ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ τοῦ μόνου διδασκάλου ἡμῶν
choices.english: disciples of Jesus Christ, our only teacher
choices.why: The genitive chain identifies Jesus Christ as the sole teacher; the rendering keeps the appositional force clear.
rejected: disciples of Jesus Christ the only teacher of us

choices.why: The adverb δικαίως modifies the waiting; 'righteously' preserves the moral quality of the prophets' expectation.

pass_b_english: If those who lived in the old ways came to a new hope, no longer keeping the Sabbath but living according to the Lord's day, on which our life also dawned through him and through his death, a death some deny, through which mystery we received faith, and because of this we endure, so that we may be found disciples of Jesus Christ, our only teacher, then how will we be able to live without him? Even the prophets, who were his disciples in the Spirit, awaited him as their teacher. And because of this, the one whom they righteously awaited came and raised them from the dead.

problems.why: παρὼν means 'being present,' not 'when he came'; temporal clause changes meaning.
problems.ruling: παρὼν is participle 'being present,' not 'when he came'; temporal clause misrenders the participle's meaning.

edits.old: when he came, raised them from the dead
edits.new: being present, raised them from the dead

problems.quote: through which mystery we received the ability to believe
problems.source_quote: δἰ οὗ μυστηρίου ἐλάβομεν τὸ πιστεύειν
problems.why: τὸ πιστεύειν is 'faith' or 'believing,' not 'ability to believe'; adds modal sense absent in source.
problems.fix: through which mystery we received faith
problems.ruling: ἐλάβομεν τὸ πιστεύειν = 'we received faith/believing'; 'ability to believe' adds modal sense not in source.

edits.old: through which mystery we received the ability to believe
edits.new: through which mystery we received faith

fixed: The 'being present, raised them from the dead' edit was not needed; the current English already matches the source.

problems.quote: If, then, those who lived in the old ways came to a new hope, no longer keeping the Sabbath but living according to the Lord's day, on which our life also dawned through him and through his death, which some deny, through which mystery we received faith, and because of this we endure, so that we may be found disciples of Jesus Christ, our only teacher: how will we be able to live without him, when even the prophets, being his disciples in the Spirit, awaited him as their teacher? And because of this, the one whom they righteously awaited, being present, raised them from the dead.
problems.why: Entire paragraph is duplicated verbatim; reader is confused by repetition.

problems.quote: through which mystery we received faith, and because of this we endure, so that we may be found disciples
problems.why: Sentence is a tangled chain of relative clauses; antecedents are unclear.
problems.fix: Break into shorter sentences; clarify what 'which mystery' refers to.

edits.old: through which mystery we received faith, and because of this we endure, so that we may be found disciples
edits.new: through this mystery we received faith, and because of this we endure, so that we may be found disciples

fixed: The antecedent of 'which mystery' is clarified by changing 'through which mystery' to 'through this mystery,' referring back to the death of Christ just mentioned.

problems.quote: on which our life also dawned through him and through his death, which some deny, through this mystery we received faith
problems.why: Clause 'which some deny' interrupts flow awkwardly; referent of 'this mystery' is unclear.
problems.fix: Reposition: 'his death—which some deny—and through this mystery...'

edits.old: through him and through his death, which some deny, through this mystery we received faith
edits.new: through him and through his death—which some deny—and through this mystery we received faith

fixed: Repositioned 'which some deny' as a parenthetical after 'his death' and clarified 'this mystery' by adding 'and' before 'through this mystery', matching the source's 'δἰ οὗ μυστηρίου' (through which mystery) referring to the death.

last_rejected.why: Glossary requires 'Lord's Day' capitalized as fixed term for κυριακή.
last_rejected.fix: living according to the Lord's Day
last_rejected.ruling: Capitalization preference, not a meaning change; 'Lord's day' adequately renders κυριακὴν.

last_rejected.quote: the one whom they righteously awaited, being present, raised them from the dead
last_rejected.source_quote: ὃν δικαίως ἀνέμενον, παρὼν ἤγειρεν αὐτοὺς ἐκ νεκρῶν
last_rejected.why: παρών is nominative, agreeing with ὃν (Christ), not the prophets; 'being present' should modify Christ.
last_rejected.fix: the one whom they righteously awaited raised them from the dead, being present
last_rejected.ruling: English 'being present' already modifies 'the one whom' (Christ), matching παρών nominative correctly.

polish.changed: The source text is a single continuous passage with no paragraph breaks or dialogue shifts; the English rendering is already clear and faithful, so no changes were needed beyond confirming the existing translation.

notes.why: Technical term for Sunday; not explained as Christian replacement of Sabbath.
notes.fix: Note: 'Sunday, the day of Christ's resurrection, replacing the Jewish Sabbath.'

polish.changed: I clarified the flow of the long conditional sentence by keeping the parenthetical denial attached to Christ's death, making the antecedent of 'this mystery' clear as the death of Christ through which faith came, and preserving the rhetorical question and final statement about the prophets intact.

notes.quote: on which our life also dawned through him and through his death, which some deny, through this mystery we received faith
notes.why: Clause 'which some deny' interrupts flow awkwardly; referent of 'this mystery' is unclear.
notes.fix: Reposition: 'his death—which some deny—and through this mystery...'

polish.changed: Clarified the Lord's day as Sunday, split long sentences, made pronoun references explicit, and smoothed the flow for reading aloud while preserving every claim and Scripture reference.

notes.why: First occurrence of term; reader may not know it means Sunday.
notes.fix: Note that 'the Lord's day' means Sunday, the day of resurrection.

polish.changed: Combined the conditional and question into one clear sentence, clarified that the prophets awaited Christ as their teacher, and removed the awkward paragraph break while preserving every claim and reference.

notes.why: First extant Christian use of 'Lord's Day' for Sunday; reader may miss significance.
notes.fix: Add note: 'the first Christian reference to Sunday as the Lord's Day'.
